We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(2{x}^{2})(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})(4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+2\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+2\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+2(\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{4}+D) \\  & =-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=2D.$

Finally, then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={[-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =(-{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )}{2}) \\  & \,-(-(0)^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+(0)\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}-\frac{1}{2})-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}-1 \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}-1\end{aligned}
$$
